formulations.label: Nebuliser solution (single-dose vials)
formulations.strengths: 250 micrograms in 1 mL, 500 micrograms in 2 mL (0.025%)
formulations.note: For inhalation with a nebuliser only; must not be taken by mouth or injected.

src.q: Each single dose unit contains 0.025 % w/v ipratropium bromide i.e. 250 micrograms in 1 ml and 500 micrograms in 2 ml.
must not be taken orally or administered parenterally

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Reversible bronchospasm in COPD; with an inhaled beta2-agonist, reversible airways obstruction in acute and chronic asthma.

src.q: indicated for treatment of reversible bronchospasm associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
when used concomitantly with inhaled beta2-agonists, for treatment of reversible airways obstruction as in acute and chronic asthma

items.t: Children and adolescents with asthma: home nebuliser rescue treatment should be started and managed only by respiratory specialists; buying a nebuliser privately for this is not recommended.

src.q: Only specialists in respiratory medicine should initiate and clinically manage use of nebulisers and associated nebulised medicines at home for acute treatment of asthma in children and adolescents.
only specialists in asthma should initiate and clinically manage use of nebulisers and associated nebulised medicines at home for acute treatment of asthma in children and adolescents

items.t: First doses should be given under close medical supervision.

src.q: Use of the nebuliser solution should be subject to close medical supervision during initial dosing.

items.t: 250-500 micrograms 3 to 4 times daily. Acute bronchospasm: 500 micrograms, repeated until stable. More than 2 mg a day only under medical supervision.
items.tag: Adults (including elderly) and adolescents over 12 years

src.q: 250 - 500 micrograms (i.e. one vial of 250 micrograms in 1 ml or 1 vial of 500 micrograms in 2 ml) 3 to 4 times daily.
For treatment of acute bronchospasm, 500 micrograms. Repeated doses can be administered until the patient is stable.
Daily doses exceeding 2 mg in adults and adolescents > 12 years of age should only be given under medical supervision.

items.t: Children 12 years and under: use only the 250 micrograms in 1 mL vial.

src.q: In children aged 12 years and under, only ATROVENT 250 UDVs, 1 ml should be used.

items.t: 6-12 years: 250 micrograms per dose, up to 1 mg a day.

src.q: Children 6 - 12 years of age: 250 micrograms (i.e. one vial of 250 micrograms in 1ml) up to a total daily dose of 1mg (4 vials).

items.t: 0-5 years (acute asthma only): 125-250 micrograms per dose, up to 1 mg a day, no more often than every 6 hours.

src.q: Children 0 - 5 years of age (for treatment of acute asthma only): 125 - 250 micrograms (i.e. half to one vial of 250 micrograms in 1 ml) up to a total daily dose of 1 mg (4 vials).
Ipratropium bromide should be administered no more frequently than 6 hourly in children under 5 years of age.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to atropine or its derivatives (including ipratropium) or any other component.

src.q: contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to atropine or its derivatives (such as the active substance ipratropium bromide) or to any other component of the product

items.t: Narrow-angle glaucoma or predisposition: use with caution; keep mist out of the eyes (mouthpiece preferred, or a well-fitting mask). Eye pain, blurred vision, haloes and red eye may signal acute glaucoma: start miotic drops and get specialist advice at once.

src.q: Caution is advocated in the use of anticholinergic agents in patients predisposed to or with narrow-angle glaucoma.
treatment with miotic drops should be initiated and specialist advice sought immediately
It is recommended that the nebulised solution is administered via a mouthpiece.

items.t: Use with caution in urinary outflow obstruction (for example prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-outflow obstruction).

src.q: should be used with caution in patients with pre-existing urinary outflow tract obstruction (e.g. prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-outflow obstruction)

items.t: Use with caution in cystic fibrosis (gut motility problems).

src.q: As patients with cystic fibrosis may be prone to gastro-intestinal motility disturbances, ATROVENT, as with other anticholinergics, should be used with caution in these patients.

items.t: Paradoxical bronchospasm can occur: treat with a fast-acting bronchodilator, stop ipratropium at once and assess.

src.q: This should be treated straight away with a fast acting inhaled bronchodilator. ATROVENT UDVs should be discontinued immediately

items.t: Long-term use with other anticholinergic medicines has not been studied and is not recommended.

src.q: Therefore, the chronic co-administration of ATROVENT with other anticholinergic drugs is not recommended.

items.t: Beta-adrenergic drugs and xanthines may add to the bronchodilator effect. Nebulising with a beta2-agonist at the same time may raise the risk of acute glaucoma in patients with a history of narrow-angle glaucoma.

src.q: There is evidence that the administration of ATROVENT with beta-adrenergic drugs and xanthine preparations may produce an additive bronchodilatory effect.
may be increased when nebulised ipratropium bromide and beta2-agonists are administered simultaneously

items.t: Do not mix in the same nebuliser with sodium cromoglicate solutions that contain benzalkonium chloride (precipitation).

src.q: should not be administered simultaneously in the same nebuliser as precipitation may occur

renal.note: No renal dose advice in the UK nebuliser solution SmPC checked.

hepatic.note: No hepatic dose advice in the UK nebuliser solution SmPC checked.

items.t: Safety in human pregnancy not established; weigh benefit against possible harm to the unborn child. Animal studies showed no embryotoxic or teratogenic effects.

src.q: The safety of ATROVENT during human pregnancy has not been established.
The benefits of using ATROVENT during a confirmed or suspected pregnancy must be weighed against the possible hazards to the unborn child.

items.t: Not known if it enters breast milk; unlikely to reach the infant in important amounts, but use with caution.

src.q: It is unlikely that ipratropium bromide would reach the infant to an important extent, however caution should be exercised when ATROVENT is administered to nursing mothers.

items.t: No human fertility data; animal studies showed no effect on fertility.

src.q: Clinical data on fertility are not available for ipratropium bromide.

items.t: Headache, dizziness, throat irritation, cough, dry mouth, nausea, gut motility changes (diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting).

src.q: The most frequent side effects reported in clinical trials were headache, throat irritation, cough, dry mouth, gastro-intestinal motility disorders (including constipation, diarrhoea and vomiting), nausea, and dizziness

items.t: Immediate hypersensitivity (urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, oropharyngeal oedema, anaphylaxis).

src.q: Immediate hypersensitivity reactions following the use of ATROVENT have been demonstrated by cases of urticaria, angioedema, rash, bronchospasm, oropharyngeal oedema and anaphylaxis.

items.t: Acute narrow-angle glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision, haloes, red eye) if mist enters the eyes: miotic drops and urgent specialist advice.

src.q: Eye pain or discomfort, blurred vision, visual halos or coloured images in association with red eyes from conjunctival congestion and corneal oedema may be signs of acute narrow-angle glaucoma.

items.t: Paradoxical bronchospasm; urinary retention (higher risk with outflow obstruction); supraventricular tachycardia or atrial fibrillation (uncommon/rare).

src.q: Paradoxical bronchospasm(2) Uncommon
Supraventricular tachycardia Uncommon Atrial fibrillation Rare
the risk of urinary retention may be increased in patients with pre-existing urinary outflow tract obstruction

items.t: Close medical supervision during the first doses.

src.q: Use of the nebuliser solution should be subject to close medical supervision during initial dosing.

items.t: Stop at once if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs.

src.q: ATROVENT UDVs should be discontinued immediately, the patient assessed and, if necessary, alternative treatment instituted.

items.t: Use with a suitable nebuliser; dilute only with sterile sodium chloride 0.9% if needed (usual final volume 2-4 mL). Can be mixed with a short-acting beta2-agonist in the same chamber; use as soon as possible after mixing.

src.q: if dilution is necessary use only sterile sodium chloride 0.9% solution
ATROVENT UDVs may be combined with a short-acting beta2-agonist in the same nebuliser chamber

items.t: Prefer a mouthpiece; if a mask is used it must fit well. Keep the solution and mist out of the eyes.

src.q: Care must be taken not to allow the solution or mist to enter the eyes.
If this is not available and a nebuliser mask is used, it must fit properly.

items.t: Get medical help at once if breathlessness is sudden or rapidly worsening. For children, seek urgent help if asthma is not relieved by rescue medicines, even after short-term improvement.

src.q: The patient should be instructed that in the case of acute or rapidly worsening dyspnoea a physician should be consulted immediately.
Urgent medical assistance should be sought if worsening asthma symptoms are not relieved by rescue medicines

items.t: May cause dizziness, blurred vision or focusing problems; if so, avoid driving or operating machinery.

src.q: If patients experience the above mentioned side effects they should avoid potentially hazardous tasks such as driving or operating machinery.

items.t: Patients prone to glaucoma should protect their eyes.

src.q: Patients who may be predisposed to glaucoma should be warned specifically to protect their eyes.
